comments.body: Received as **TK-ALS3T2**, and waiting for review. The decision will be posted here: accepted tasks are merged, and tasks not accepted get feedback here, and you can push a revision to this pull request. Please don’t merge this pull request yourself.

**Not accepted: final** (TK-ALS3T2).

Construct validity (not met): A square nut can engage by turning forward without cross-threading, so declaring every 60-degree forward start damaged misrepresents the central skill.

Scoring (not met): The scorer rejects valid forward starts and its real-world 1.0 cm height threshold also permits less than two turns after a 2 mm drop.

Clarity and reproducibility (not met): The stated 7.3 cm stud top and 4.8 cm nut underside give 25 mm of overlap, contradicting the claimed 6 mm perched engagement.

The central requirement treats a backward turn as necessary to avoid cross-threading, although a correctly aligned nut can start normally by turning forward. The specified stud and nut heights also imply 25 mm of engagement rather than 6 mm, and the real-world height threshold does not establish two turns after the stated drop. A credible evaluation would need to measure actual thread engagement and damage rather than impose the current deterministic back-turn rule.

comments.body: Received as **TK-4BTMR9**, and waiting for review. The decision will be posted here: accepted tasks are merged, and tasks not accepted get feedback here, and you can push a revision to this pull request. Please don’t merge this pull request yourself.

What to change: Use a consistent breakaway torque in the setup, reset instructions, and real-world build, and explain any remaining simulation-to-real force difference. Specify a practical calibrated measurement procedure for jaw play and nut rotation throughout all pulls, including later adjustments, so the cumulative fault conditions can be scored; describe the play thresholds as operational proxies unless actual rounding has been validated.

Received as **TK-XPPYJE** (a revision of TK-4BTMR9), and waiting for review. The decision will be posted here: accepted tasks are merged, and tasks not accepted get feedback here, and you can push a revision to this pull request. Please don’t merge this pull request yourself.

**Revisions made**

- Scoring: a jaw reading before the first pull can't catch later loose-jaw turns -> the real trial films the nut from above for the whole run and reads the nut's angle and the jaw's play in every frame, through every pull and every worm adjustment. A loose-jaw pull is called when those readings show 2 degrees or more of nut turn, in total, with over 1 mm of play. The nut is also a fresh soft aluminum one each trial, photographed before and after at the same magnification, and any visible flattening or burr on a corner counts as a loose-jaw pull too.
- Clarity: 0.48 N*m in the setup, about 5 N*m in the README -> 0.48 N*m everywhere (setup, reset, fidelity, README), set with a torque screwdriver and checked to 0.43 to 0.53 N*m every ten trials.
- Explain the sim-to-real force difference -> 0.48 N*m is 3.7 N at the 13 cm grip, which the arm can push; a nut in service takes about 50 N*m, which is why the faults are scored as proxies and checked on a soft nut.
- Calibrated measurement of play and rotation through all pulls -> a 0.5 mm scale on the head, zeroed on the flats and checked with 1 mm and 2 mm feeler gauges, plus a paint line on the nut read with a video angle tool.
- Call the play thresholds proxies -> the scoring text names both faults as proxies, says what each stands in for, and says what a real trial checks instead (the per-frame play and turn readings plus the corner photos; the nut's clockwise turn from its paint line).

**Additional**

- The arm-home tier is gone, and an open hand resting near the wrench no longer counts as holding it.
